A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sheaf-FMTL work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and regression experiments, communication measurements, and heterogeneous-feature experiments in Section 4 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark comparisons, heterogeneous-CNN experiments, resource measurements, and topology and initialization analyses in Section 4 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The sheaf-regularized objective, alternating model/map updates in equations (18)–(19), and Algorithm 1 are retained. Remark 3 clarifies why initialization must be nonzero; Gaussian initialization was already documented in v1. The CNN experiments change evaluated model configurations rather than the proposed learning procedure.

E1.justification: All six underlying datasets remain, but v1's feature-dropped Vehicle classification and School regression scenarios are removed from Section 4.3 and Appendix F. Their replacement uses the already-covered image datasets. This substantially changes coverage of heterogeneous available input features; the ordinary Vehicle and School evaluations remain in Appendix G.

E2.justification: v2 adds D-PSGD and local-training comparisons to the existing main and appendix benchmark plots. Table 4 adds FedAvg and evaluates DITTO, pFedMe, and Per-FedAvg on the image datasets. The numerical Vehicle/HAR comparisons against these personalized baselines in v1 Table 2 are no longer reported, despite residual prose mentioning those datasets.

E3.justification: v1 Appendix F.2 specifies multinomial logistic regression for all classification experiments; v2 Section 4.1 specifies CNNs for image datasets and introduces three heterogeneous CNN configurations in Table 2. New protocols measure FLOPs and peak memory and vary graph topology, regularization strength, and initialization. These are substantial reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish whether retained curves were rerun.

E4.justification: New Section 4.4 tests regularization sensitivity across small-world, scale-free, and complete networks, and tests Gaussian, uniform, orthogonal, and noisy-identity map initializations. Figure 4 additionally examines learned restriction-map norms. These provide new evidence about sensitivity and learned interactions beyond v1's benchmark comparisons.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five runs, one-standard-error shading for performance curves, and mean plus standard deviation for the main multi-baseline table. No changed run count, seed scheme, confidence-interval method, or significance-testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v1's modified Vehicle/School trajectories and Vehicle/HAR comparison table are replaced by heterogeneous-CNN trajectories and image-dataset comparisons with resource measurements. v2 Table 4 reports R-MNIST accuracies of 94.3 ± 0.12 and 94.5 ± 0.08 for Sheaf-FMTL, versus 94.4 ± 0.06 for dFedU. Additional baseline curves and Tables 5–6 supply new topology and initialization results. These are added or replacement outcomes, not established same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: The sheaf definitions, special-case reductions, formal assumptions, lemmas, convergence bound, and proofs in Appendices D–E are retained. Remark 3 explains the zero-initialization failure of the existing update without revising the formal theory.

C1.justification: The central heterogeneity, unification, communication-efficiency, and convergence claims remain. v2 qualifies the abstract and contribution statements with computational/storage costs and a cross-silo focus, and removes the claimed additional privacy benefit from the introduction and conclusion. Resource costs were already acknowledged in v1 Section 4.2.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of map-norm heatmaps as selective client coupling and of initialization results as evidence of robustness. It identifies zero initialization as a failure condition and explains that favorable regularization ranges are dataset-dependent and excessive regularization can harm personalization. Resource trade-offs receive greater emphasis, while Appendix A.5's enhanced-privacy interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: v2 documents CNN layers, filter counts, approximate parameter counts, client allocation, heterogeneous projection dimensions, baseline validation-grid-search tuning, and detailed initialization alternatives. It also explains the FLOP and peak-memory measurements. Hardware, software, Gaussian initialization, and regularization values largely move from Appendix F into Section 4.1; instructions for generating the removed feature-dropped datasets disappear.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a focused taxonomy of feature, label, concept, and quantity heterogeneity with additional literature, including Hsieh et al., Kairouz et al., and Li et al. The D-PSGD comparison introduces Lian et al. Existing positioning as a sheaf generalization of graph-based FMTL remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially rewritten and reorganized. Settings and hardware information move from Appendix F into an expanded Section 4.1, Section 4.3 is rewritten around heterogeneous CNNs, and Section 4.4 introduces two analysis subsections. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are also revised around cross-silo applicability and resource trade-offs.

P2.justification: v2 replaces Figure 3, removes the old model-size histogram, adds restriction-map heatmaps and topology diagrams, and introduces architecture and ablation tables. The main comparison table gains FLOP and memory columns, and benchmark plots gain baseline curves and legends. Appendix tables gain model and heterogeneity-type columns; the supplementary figure caption corrects the HAR/School row labels.

improvement.justification: The heterogeneous-CNN tests, additional baselines, and topology/initialization analyses strengthen empirical scrutiny, while removing unsupported enhanced-privacy claims improves qualification. The net gain is limited by losing direct feature-dropping tests and introducing reporting inconsistencies: Section 4.2 says D-PSGD struggles to exceed 55% on H-CIFAR-10, while Figure 2 and Table 4 show about 64%, and its communication discussion mixes KB with Table 4's MB units. These problems weaken the otherwise useful expansion.
